title: Advanced Scientific & Humanities Lexicon
description: High-level CEFR C1/C2 vocabulary distinguishing legitimate scholarly terms from deceptive morphological inventions.

words.explanation: 'anachronistic' is a real adjective meaning belonging or appropriate to a period other than that in which it exists.
'obfuscatory' is a real adjective meaning intended to render obscure, unclear, or unintelligible.
'epistemology' is the philosophical study of the nature, origin, and limits of human knowledge.
'perfunctation' is an invented pseudo-word; standard English uses 'perfunctoriness'.
'vicissitude' is a real noun referring to a change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome.
'superfinitude' is an invented pseudo-philosophical term combining 'super' and 'finitude'.
'pusillanimous' is a real adjective meaning showing a lack of courage or determination; timid.
'circumspection' is a real noun meaning the quality of being wary and unwilling to take risks; prudence.
'ineffability' is a real noun meaning the quality of being too great or extreme to be expressed in words.
'bellicosement' is an invented pseudo-noun; standard English uses 'bellicosity'.
'sesquipedalian' is a real adjective describing words containing many syllables or using long words.
'taciturnity' is a real noun meaning the state or quality of being reserved or uncommunicative in speech.
'quintessial' is an invalid pseudo-word; the genuine word is 'quintessential'.
'idiosyncrasy' is a real noun meaning a mode of behavior or way of thought peculiar to an individual.
'malleability' is a real noun meaning the ability of a substance to be molded, hammered, or adapted.
'inadvisability' is a real noun meaning the state of being unwisely chosen or not recommended.
'concurrencehood' is an invented pseudo-word; standard English uses 'concurrence'.
'propitiousness' is a real noun indicating a favorable, auspicious, or advantageous disposition.
